title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatises a 'magasin' (store) M. This is a set of geometric pieces (for example points and segments, or cells) carrying several relations.

The relations, as inferred from their use on this page and the next:
- X ≤ Y is a partial order ('X is a face of Y'). Write X̃ = M_{≤X}.
- X ≪ Y is a second relation ('X lies in Y'). It is antisymmetric by Mag 1.
- X ≪̊ Y means X ≪ Y and Y is ≤-minimal with this property: X ≪ Y' ≤ Y implies Y' = Y. So Y is the 'carrier' of X, the piece in whose interior X lies.
- X |0| Y means 'X and Y are disjoint'. By Mag 3 a) it is irreflexive (and symmetric). By Mag 3 b) it is inherited: X |0| Y and X' ≪̊ X imply X' |0| Y.
- Mag 2 says: if Z ≪ Y, there is Y' with Z ≪̊ Y' ≤ Y.
- Mag 4 is a 'linearity' axiom for 'M linéaires', i.e. 1-dimensional stores. It says two distinct (incomparable) faces of one Y are disjoint, like the two endpoints of a segment.
- X ≭ Y ('X and Y are compatible / in general position') means: every X'' ∈ X̃ \ (X̃∩Ỹ) and every Y'' ∈ Ỹ \ (X̃∩Ỹ) satisfy X''|0|Y''. In words, X and Y meet only along common faces.

On the previous page a figure is defined as a ≤-closed set of pairwise compatible elements, i.e. a subcomplex. This page, dated 27 June, inserts preliminary lemmas on linear magasins before treating figures.

Prop 1:
- a) ≭ is symmetric and reflexive; this is trivial from the definition and Mag 3 a).
- b) ≭ descends to faces: X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y and X ≭ Y imply X' ≭ Y'.
- Proof of b): take X'' and Y'' outside X̃'∩Ỹ'. If neither lies in X̃∩Ỹ, use the definition of X ≭ Y. If X'' ∈ X̃∩Ỹ, then X'' and Y'' are distinct (indeed incomparable) faces of Y, so Mag 4 gives disjointness.

Prop 2 (margin): if X ≭ Y and X ≠ Y (with X, Y incomparable), then X |0| Y. The converse holds by Mag 3 a).

Cor 1: if X ≭ Y and Z ≪̊ X, then Z ≪ Y ⇔ X ≪ Y.

Cor 2: if Z ≪̊ X, Z ≪̊ Y and X ≭ Y, then X = Y. Compatible pieces sharing an interior point coincide.

The final proof of Cor 1:
1. By Mag 2 take Y' with Z ≪̊ Y' ≤ Y.
2. By Prop 1 b), X ≭ Y'.
3. This reduces the question to Cor 2.
4. Cor 2 is proved directly: if X ≠ Y', Prop 2 gives X |0| Y'. Mag 3 b) applied twice then gives Z |0| Z, contradicting Mag 3 a).

Purpose: this is the basic incidence calculus needed to show that figures (subcomplexes) inherit ≤ and ≪ well. On the next page it yields Cor 3 (under ≭, X ≪ Y ⇔ X ≤ Y) and the analogous statements for figures.
errors: The first justification of Cor 2 ('on aura X≪Y et Y≪X, donc X=Y par Mag 1') uses Cor 1, while the proof of Cor 1 is then reduced to Cor 2. Taken together this is circular. Grothendieck resolves it at the bottom of the page with a direct proof of Cor 2 via Prop 2 and Mag 3 b).

Prop 2 as needed (X ≭ Y, X ≠ Y ⇒ X|0|Y) is false if X < Y, because then X ≭ Y holds vacuously but X and Y are not disjoint. It needs X and Y incomparable. In the application this follows from Z ≪̊ X and Z ≪̊ Y (minimality of the carriers), but the page does not say so.
In the proof of Prop 1 b), the symmetric case Y'' ∈ X̃∩Ỹ is not written; it is 'by symmetry'. The incomparability of X'' and Y'' needed for Mag 4 is also only implicit.
Cor 1's conclusion X ≪ Y from X = Y' ≤ Y tacitly uses that ≤ implies ≪ (or that ≪ is reflexive and compatible with ≤). This is not stated here.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'magasin': a poset of cells with an incidence relation ≪, a carrier relation ≪̊ and a disjointness relation |0|, used as a combinatorial foundation for tame/polyhedral topology
ideas.modern_name: abstract cell complexes / face posets with incidence axioms; o-minimal-style cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abstract cell complexes: Tucker, Steinitz; regular CW posets: Björner; tame topology: van den Dries and others
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6). The 'magasin' axiomatics itself appears only in these archive notes, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Compatibility X ≭ Y (meeting only along common faces), its stability under passing to faces, and 'compatible cells with a common interior point are equal'
ideas.modern_name: general position / intersection along a common face, as in the definition of a simplicial or polyhedral complex

missed.claim: The page belongs to an unpublished axiomatisation ('magasins', with 'figures' as compatible closed subsets) of 1-dimensional and polyhedral tame topology. It differs from existing cell-complex axiomatics in taking 'interior incidence' ≪ and disjointness as primitives. The lemmas on this page are routine, but the framework as a whole has not been developed in the literature.
missed.quote: Avant de passer aux figures, il faudrait donner quelques compléments sur M linéaires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible combinatorial foundation for the tame topology programme of the Esquisse, comparable with o-minimal cell decompositions. Historians studying Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' may value the precise axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary order-theoretic lemmas inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework is of historical interest, but the content of this page is routine.
transcription_corrections: Margin Prop 2 should read roughly 'Si X≭Y, X≠Y ⇒ X|0|Y' (with the converse X|0|Y ⇒ X≠Y), not only 'X|0|Y ⇒ X≠Y'. The direction X≠Y ⇒ X|0|Y is the one used in the text ('on aurait par prop 2 X|0|Y').
'Prouvons X''|0|Y''' at the end of the Dém a) line belongs to the start of part b).
In b), the condition is likely 'Y'' ∈ Ỹ' \ X̃'∩Ỹ''. In the second case the text reads 'on a X'' ∈ Ỹ, Y'' ∈ Ỹ' ⊂ Ỹ, d'autre part évidemment X''≠Y''' (as transcribed).
